Automated testing, for beginners

AI writes code quickly and sounds confident when it is wrong. Automated tests are how you find out which is which, and Claude can write them for you.

Why bother in a four-hour hackathon?

A test is a small program that checks your program. You write it once and it re-checks your work every time anything changes, in seconds.

With an AI agent, tests do double duty: Claude can run them itself after every edit and fix what it broke before you ever see it. Asking for tests is the single best way to make an agent's work trustworthy.

For civic data they matter even more. A chart that is off by a factor of ten looks exactly as convincing as a correct one.

The kinds of test

Many small fast tests at the bottom, a few slow thorough ones at the top.

Test suites and the tools for each
KindChecksPython toolJavaScript / web tool
UnitA single function returns the right answerpytestnode --test, Vitest, Jest
DataColumns, types, ranges, row counts, no duplicatespytest + pandas, pandera—
IntegrationPieces work together end to end, without a browserpytestnode --test
End-to-endA real browser can load, click, and see resultsPlaywright for PythonPlaywright
AccessibilityKeyboard use, contrast, labels for screen readersPlaywright + axeaxe-core, Lighthouse
LoadThe site stays fast when many people visit at onceLocustk6, autocannon
Continuous integrationAll of the above run on every push, automaticallyGitHub ActionsGitHub Actions

Your first test: check the data

Put this in tests/test_trees.py, run python -m pytest, and watch it pass or tell you exactly what is wrong. Or ask Claude: write data tests like these for our dataset.

Let Claude test its own work

The pattern is called test-driven development: describe what right looks like, let the test fail, then let Claude make it pass.

  1. Describe the behaviour

    Write a pytest test for a function share_by_genus(df) that returns each genus's share of all trees, summing to 100%. Don't write the function yet.

  2. Watch it fail

    Run the test and show me it fails. A failing test proves the test actually checks something.

  3. Make it pass

    Now write the function until the test passes. Don't change the test.

  4. Keep it running

    Add a line to CLAUDE.md: Run python -m pytest before every commit. Claude will check its own work from then on.

End-to-end: a robot clicks your page

Install with pip install pytest-playwright then playwright install chromium. Or add the Playwright connector from the toolbox and just ask Claude to click around.

Run every test on every push

Save this as .github/workflows/ci.yml in your repository. GitHub runs your tests each time you push, and shows a green tick or a red cross on every commit.

A real example: this site

The showcase you are reading is tested the same way. Browse its tests for working examples.

How the Day in Our Data showcase is tested
SuiteWhat it guards
tests/test_*.py (pytest)Vote counting, ranking, ID stability, workflow safety, and that these guide pages match their TOML source.
tests/js/*.test.js (node:test)The results page escapes untrusted text and renders ties and edge cases correctly.
tests/e2e/ (Playwright + axe)Every page loads without errors, works at phone width, passes automated accessibility checks, and has no broken internal links.
tests/load/ (Locust)The static pages stay fast with a room full of people loading them at once.
GitHub ActionsRuns the suites on every push and pull request.

Found a mistake? These pages are built from guides/pages/testing.toml in the showcase repository. Pull requests welcome.
